The Past Perfect in Narrative Sequence
The Past Perfect can be used to talk about sequences of events. You can use the Past Perfect in a narrative when you want to write more eloquently and make your style of writing more dynamic.

You use the Past Perfect to talk about an event that was completed before another past event. Therefore, it is often connected to a Simple Past event. You use the Past Perfect with conjunctions such as and, that, because, so and when, or prepositions such as as before and as already.

I had left my laptop at home so I did not study in the library.
He had put on too much cologne before he went out.
They had brought back so much garlic that the whole house smelled when we arrived.
The Past Perfect event finished before the Simple Past event.

Like other perfect tenses, the Past Perfect often has a connection to, or impact on, the event that it is linked to. In all of the above examples, the Past Perfect affects the Simple Past event. If it did not have an impact on the following event, we could use the Simple Past.
You use the Past Perfect to talk about how long something happened before another event in the past. You use the preposition for to talk about duration.

We had had that car for ten years before it broke down.
By the time Nate finished school, he had been in New York for over eight years.
For many years a man, his wife, and their little son had lived together happily in a little village in China.
By the time the sun rose again, he had died.
I am only holding this axe, which Father had given to me before he died.
He had been so jealous that he had not thought about the young man's sorrow.
The Participle Clause: The Past Participle
You can use participle clauses after a noun in the same way as relative clauses. This gives more information about the noun.
A past participle can be used in the same way as a Simple Past passive relative clause:

We read the email sent by the company.
(= We read the email that had been sent by the company).

This vase, made in China in the 14th century, is very beautiful.
(= This vase, which was made in China in the 14th century, is very beautiful).

He only eats cakes made by his mother.
(= He only eats cakes that are made by his mother).

images.text:
For many years a man, his wife, and their little son had lived together happily in a little village in China. The father was a woodsman and used a great axe to chop down trees. One day, the father became very ill. He called his son and said, "I want you to take good care of your mother, for she is a good woman. And here is something for you.
Take this axe. Whenever you are sad and lonely, hold it and you will feel my strength, the strength I had when I was young." By the time the sun rose again, he had died. The boy was very sad and he treasured the axe given to him by his father

The young man missed his father greatly. His mother, filled with loneliness, married again. The new husband, consumed by jealousy, hated the son.
When the new husband saw the young man holding the axe, he said to his wife, "Your son is thinking about killing me. He is going to use that axe."
This angered the mother and she asked her son, "Why are you trying to kill your stepfather?"
The son replied, "I am only holding this axe, which Father had given to me before he died. He told me I could always feel his strength in it. Do not worry. I would never try to kill your husband. I love you too much to hurt anyone that you love."

The woman understood and loved her son even more because of his love for both his father and his mother. She too felt the empty space left by the father's death. Even the stepfather felt regret and said, "I am sorry. Please forgive me." He had been so jealous that he had not thought about the young man's sorrow.
The son forgave him and the family lived together in peace. Whenever the young man wanted to feel the strength of his father, he held his father's axe.
